When a station is asleep
column2: the fw will set it as ""asleep"".

column1: All queues that are used only by one station will be stopped by
the fw.
In pre-DQA mode this was relevant for aggregation queues. However
in DQA mode a queue is owned by one station only
will be stopped.
As a result
column2: we don't expect to get filtered frames back to

column1: mac80211 and don't have to maintain the entire pending_frames
state logic
column2: the same way as we do in aggregations.

column1: The correct behavior is to align DQA behavior with the aggregation
queue behaviour pre-DQA:
- Don't count pending frames.
- Let mac80211 know we have frames in these queues so that it can
properly handle trigger frames.
When a trigger frame is received
column2: mac80211 tells the driver to send

column1: frames from the queues using release_buffered_frames.
The driver will tell the fw to let frames out even if the station
is asleep. This is done by iwl_mvm_sta_modify_sleep_tx_count.
